sources_and_data.use: Preserved the Multiway-Cut feasibility gate, the O7 negative route, and the contraction-only/arbitrary-sparsifier boundary.
Retained the exact cost-plus-crossing objective and arbitrary finite-metric quantifiers.
Complete exposition and proof audit for this task.

method.type: direct mathematical derivation and adversarial proof audit; no experiment or network search
method.interface: I_N(q;a,b,rho): minimum metric-labeling cost with boundary labels, prescribed internal terminal assignment rho, and at most q crossings
method.quantifiers: finite two-terminal series-parallel multigraphs for the full interface, and arbitrary finite unweighted multigraphs for the terminal-free scalar sublemma; arbitrary finite metrics, injective ambient terminal labels, and every finite crossing budget
method.composition: series is min-plus convolution over the glued label and split budget; parallel is min-plus convolution over split budget with fixed shared boundary labels
method.terminal_free_reduction: I_N(q;a,b)=lambda_N*mu(a,b) when a!=b and q>=lambda_N, with lambda_N the two-terminal edge connectivity; the proof is a standard metric/min-cut consequence for any finite unweighted host

assumptions: Graphs are finite undirected multigraphs; parallel edges count separately and loops contribute zero cost and zero crossings.
The two boundary vertices are interface vertices and are not silently treated as terminals unless their labels are fixed by the ambient instance.
Internal terminal assignments are held fixed in the general interface I_N; the terminal-free scalar reduction is claimed only when the internal terminal set is empty.
The metric is finite and satisfies symmetry, positivity on distinct labels, and the triangle inequality.
This is a mathematical proof audit only; no experiment, network search, or experiment-budget renewal occurred.
Any contraction-only consequence remains separate from arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.
verified_steps: The general table I_N(q;a,b,rho) is defined with an at-most crossing budget, so it is finite and exact for every fixed finite metric and fixed internal terminal assignment.
For series composition, cutting a labeling at the glued vertex gives a shared label z and a crossing split q_A+q_B<=q; gluing two minimizing labelings gives the reverse inequality.
For parallel composition, restrictions to each branch share the same two boundary labels and their crossing counts add; conversely branch minimizers glue without any new boundary edge.

For a terminal-free module, constant labeling is feasible when endpoints agree, while endpoint disagreement forces at least lambda_N crossings and triangle inequality lower-bounds cost by lambda_N*mu(a,b). The edgewise absolute-difference sum is integrated over [0,infinity) and only then truncated to [0,mu(a,b)]; a minimum cut attains equality.
The feasible path with one internal terminal separates connectivity information from the metric label needed at that terminal, refuting scalar endpoint/connectivity closure.
gaps: No label-independent representative-set compression for terminal-bearing series-parallel modules has been proved.
The exact general table can have a factor |D|^(|R_N|+2), so no universal-exponent-free sparsifier size follows from the interface theorem.
No feasible superlinear contraction-only lower bound was proved, and no statement transfers to arbitrary sparsifiers.
The terminal-free scalar interface is a restricted structural result, not an unrestricted Zero Extension theorem.

counterexamples.claim_refuted: Endpoint labels, two-terminal connectivity, and a crossing budget alone form an exact label-independent interface for every series-parallel module.
counterexamples.witness: The path s-x-t with x an internal terminal labelled c has cost mu(a,c)+mu(c,b) and crossing count 1[a!=c]+1[c!=b]. Two valid metrics with the same mu(a,b)=2 give sums 3 and 4, so endpoint distance and connectivity do not determine the exact table.
counterexamples.feasibility: With all three vertices terminal and injective labels, the instance is feasible for k>=2: both path edges must be crossing edges, and deleting both edges is a terminal Multiway Cut. It is infeasible for k<2.

proof_status.scope: The exact general interface and its series/parallel composition laws are established; terminal-free scalar closure is established; scalar closure for internal-terminal modules is refuted.
excluded_claims: No label-independent polynomial sparsifier bound for all series-parallel graphs is claimed.
No superlinear contraction-only lower bound is claimed.
No transfer to arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers is claimed.

independent_review.review_type: adversarial two-sided review of series/parallel composition, terminal-free reduction, and internal-terminal obstruction
reviewed_failure_modes: forgetting the shared glued label in series composition
forgetting that parallel branch crossing counts add
using exactly-q instead of at-most-q semantics
silently treating boundary vertices as terminals
claiming scalar closure after an internal terminal is introduced
confusing a finite interface table with a label-independent sparsifier bound
independent_review.review_conclusion: Equations (S) and (P) are exact under the stated assumptions, while the path s-x-t is a valid feasible obstruction to scalar label-independent closure. The remaining compression question is open.

mathematical_claim: The full cost/crossing interface composes exactly in both series and parallel directions. A label-independent scalar interface is exact for terminal-free two-terminal modules, including non-cactus series-parallel graphs, but cannot extend to modules containing internal terminals without retaining their metric labels or an equivalent label-dependent state.

observed_result_or_blocker.positive_result: Equations (S) and (P) are proved in both directions for arbitrary finite metrics and preserve the global crossing budget exactly.
observed_result_or_blocker.concrete_feasible_obstruction: The three-terminal path s-x-t has two-terminal connectivity 1 but exact interface cost mu(a,c)+mu(c,b) and crossing requirement 1[a!=c]+1[c!=b]; a scalar state retaining only endpoint labels, connectivity, and budget is not exact.
observed_result_or_blocker.scope_blocker: The exact general table has up to (k+1)|D|^(|R_N|+2) raw entries, so no hidden-label-exponent-free representative bound was established for terminal-bearing series-parallel modules.
observed_result_or_blocker.status: bounded interface theorem proved; unrestricted series-parallel sparsifier-size question remains open

uncertainty: The obstruction refutes scalar label-independent closure, not every possible compressed interface with additional metric structure.
No feasible superlinear contraction-only lower bound was proved.
No conclusion transfers from contractions to arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.
No claim is made about Paper 3 outcomes; Targets A and B remain unchanged.
next_falsifiable_action: Either construct a label-dependent interface compression whose state count has no hidden exponent in |D|, or prove that a family of terminal-bearing series-parallel modules forces such dependence; any lower-bound route must keep every instance Multiway-Cut-feasible and must not reuse pairwise-signature inference.
